name: Thierry Alet
note: Birth sources conflict: 1965 Martinique (fashion.at 2011) vs 1969 Basse-Terre, Guadeloupe (Guadeloupe 1ere listing, Fondation Clement 2024 catalogue). Lived in New York from 1995, later settled in Guadeloupe and opened a gallery.

name: Allora & Calzadilla
origin_country: USA (Jennifer Allora, b. 1974 Philadelphia) / Cuba (Guillermo Calzadilla, b. 1971 Havana)
note: Duo; no single birth year. Recent shows: Specters of Noon (Menil Collection, 2020), Chalk (Walker Art Center, 2019), The Tropical Pharmacy (Guggenheim Bilbao, 2019). Represented the USA at Venice Biennale 2011.

name: Juan Carlos Alom
note: Photographer and filmmaker. One source says he splits time between Havana and New York; Mellon Artist in Residence at NYU Hemispheric Institute 2023.

name: Hurvin Anderson
note: Sources differ: Royal Academy says Cambridgeshire; Tate and Artnet say London; Durham Press says between London and Cambridgeshire. Turner Prize shortlist 2017.

name: Janine Antoni
note: Born Freeport, Bahamas; Bahamian-born American. MacArthur Fellow 1998.

name: Deborah Anzinger
note: Maintains studios in the US and Jamaica; founder of New Local Space, Kingston. Birthplace: Kingston (own site, Ocula) vs St Andrew (Wikipedia). Shown at 35th Sao Paulo Biennial.

name: Ewan Atkinson
note: No results found for this name; search returned only unrelated Atkinsons. Nothing verified.

name: Firelei Báez
note: Birth year given as 1980 or 1981 by institutional sources. Emigrated to US aged nine, raised in Miami. Shows: Bloodlines (Perez Art Museum Miami, 2015), Joy Out of Fire (Studio Museum in Harlem, 2018), Trust Memory Over History (Kunstmuseum Wolfsburg, travelled to Louisiana Museum 2023), survey at Des Moines Art Center 2025. Represented by Hauser & Wirth.

name: Wray Banker
note: No results found for this name; search returned unrelated Wray / Banker artists. Nothing verified.

name: Abel Barroso
note: Born Pinar del Rio, Cuba; printmaker making woodcut sculptures/installations. Exhibition: Abel Barroso, Une ile a l'etranger (Fondation Clement).

name: José Bedia
note: Born Havana; in Miami since 1993 (one source mentions a Mexico stint first). Magiciens de la Terre 1989; first prize Beijing Biennale 2010.

name: La Vaughn Belle
origin_country: US Virgin Islands (born Tobago per Wikipedia; Trinidad and Tobago per other sources)

works.title: I Am Queen Mary (with Jeannette Ehlers)

note: Moved to St. Thomas as an infant. Royal Copenhagen porcelain commission.

name: Mario Benjamin
note: Self-taught; shown at Havana, Johannesburg, Venice, Sao Paulo, Dakar biennials. Made a 2011 earthquake memorial for Digicel.

name: Christian Bertin
note: Born Fort-de-France; returned to Martinique 1986; installations and performance (memory, wounds, healing). Solo shows Espace Oberkampf 2019, SERMAC 2017, Fondation Clement 2010; Liverpool Biennial 2010.

name: Edward Bowen

works.title: A Walk in the Park with Doctor Bob

note: In the Grenada Pavilion, 'The Poetics of Correspondence', 2026 Venice Biennale (to 22 Nov 2026). Solo shows: Stories 2017, Heds 2019, The Rainwater Paintings 2022 (Y Art Gallery); book Black Light Void (2024).

name: Tania Bruguera
residence: New York, USA (Queens) / Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA
note: Residence sources conflict: Queens NY (National Academy, Tate listing) vs Cambridge MA (Tate bio, Wikipedia; Harvard). Other sources say Havana/New York.

name: Ras Ishi Butcher
note: Birth year uncertain: one profile says 1965, a 1992 report calls him 33 (c.1959). Teaches in BFA programme at Barbados Community College; studied at ISA Havana 1997; gold award at first Caribbean and Central American Biennial, Santo Domingo 1992; solo show 'Isolation' 1995.

name: Holly Bynoe
note: Artist, curator, writer; co-founder ARC Magazine; former Chief Curator NAGB (to end 2019); PhD candidate at St Andrews; birth year from a single source.

name: Charles Campbell
note: Jamaican-born; moved to Prince Edward Island aged five; formerly Chief Curator, National Gallery of Jamaica; 2022 VIVA Award. Shows: Fragments of Epic Memory (AGO), The Other Side of Now (PAMM). Birth year not shown.

name: María Magdalena Campos-Pons
note: Born La Vega, Matanzas, 22 July 1959 (one infobox says August). Residence sources split: Nashville (Vanderbilt chair since 2017) vs Boston. Represented Cuba at 2013 Venice Biennale; retrospective Everything is Separated by Water (Indianapolis, 2006); 2023 MacArthur noted.

name: Liset Castillo
note: Born Camagüey; ISA Havana 1998; De Ateliers Amsterdam 2000-02; sand-based work; recent solo at TORCH Gallery, Amsterdam.
